Hi Neha —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our infra and ML platform teams would like a technical deep-dive on Redwood’s Dedicated offering focused on: pool sizing, autoscaling behavior under bursty inference workloads, and isolation strategies for multi-tenant deployments.

High level asks:
- Walk us through sizing guidance for a mix of short-form chat traffic (high qps, low seq) and long-context generation (lower qps, long seq lengths).
- How autoscaling behaves with queued requests / queue throttling and cold-start characteristics.
- Isolation primitives (tenant-level KV cache, secure GPU tenancy, noisy-neighbor mitigation).

Would you / Rishi be available next week for a 60–75 minute session? Our preferred windows: Tue/Wed/Thu (Apr 6–8) morning PT. If you can send a calendar slot and a short pre-read we’ll circulate internally.

Thanks,

Confirmed — Thu Apr 8, 11:00 PT. Thanks for the agenda and the prep. Quick answers below:
- Peak expected qps (chat): ~450 qps across the fleet during launches; typical sustained 150–200 qps.
- 95th percentile seq length (chat): ~80 tokens

- Isolation: VP prefers dedicated pools for high-value tenants, but we’re also interested in soft-isolation options for lower tiers.

We’ll be ready and have an internal document on compliance and audit access available if needed. See you on Zoom.
